transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name], and I'll be speaking with you today. Can you tell me what brings you in or what's been on your mind lately?

Yeah… I guess I came in because I feel like I can’t stop worrying. It’s not just one thing, it’s like everything is happening in my head at the same time. My marriage, whether I’m messing things up at work or starting to slip, bills, the house stuff I keep starting and then dropping… and then it all turns into this bigger thought that I’m basically failing as a husband and as a father.

I know that sounds like a lot, but it’s kind of constant. I’ll be trying to focus on something simple and my mind just jumps to all of it, like a list I can’t ever finish. And I keep thinking if I could just handle one area better, maybe the rest would calm down, but instead I just end up worrying about all of it at once.
Have you noticed that you’ve lost interest or feel less pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, like hobbies, time with family, or other things that once brought you happiness?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I don’t think it’s that I don’t enjoy things at all anymore. Like if something good is happening, I can still recognize it’s good, and I can still have moments where I’m glad to be with my family or doing something I used to like.

But it’s harder to tell because a lot of the time I’m sort of… distracted, I guess. Like I’ll be there physically, but my head is somewhere else, so it can feel like I’m not getting as much out of it. I don’t know if that counts as losing interest or pleasure, or if it’s more that I have trouble settling into anything enough to enjoy it. So I wouldn’t say I’ve clearly lost interest, no—not in a way I’ve specifically noticed.
Can you tell me if you feel like you're able to control these worries, or does it feel like they take over even when you try to push them aside?

It definitely feels like they take over. I mean, I try to control it—I really do. Like at work, I’ll tell myself, okay, just look at the code in front of you, just solve this one problem, don’t go anywhere else. But then some little concern gets in, like maybe I’m taking too long on something, and that turns into wondering if my manager has noticed, and then I’m imagining a bad review, and then somehow I’m all the way at losing my job and my family being worse off because I couldn’t keep it together.

And it happens even when I’m doing something that should help. Like if I’m working out, I’ll try to just breathe and focus on what I’m doing, but my brain doesn’t stay there. One worry hooks onto another, and before I know it I’m twenty steps ahead in some disaster scenario. It’s not like I want to think about it. I’ll push it aside and it just comes back from a different angle. So yeah, I don’t feel like I’m in control of it most of the time.
Do you ever notice physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, shaking, or feeling tense when these worries come up?

Yeah, the main thing I notice is tension. I don’t know if I’d describe it as, like, dramatic every time, but I feel wound tight almost all day. My shoulders especially—like they’re locked up or I’m bracing for something, even when there’s nothing actually happening right in front of me.

And I get restless with it too. Sitting still can feel weirdly hard. Between meetings at work I’ll catch myself pacing around, not even going anywhere, just moving because staying in the chair feels impossible. Or at chess club, I’ll be tapping the pieces or shifting around, and then I realize I’m probably being annoying, which of course gives me another thing to worry about. It’s like my body is acting like something bad is about to happen before my brain has even settled on what I’m worried about.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you found yourself feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

I don’t think so. I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m feeling cheerful or relaxed most days, but “down or depressed most of the day nearly every day” doesn’t quite feel like the right description.

There are definitely times where I feel worn out or kind of discouraged, especially if I’ve spent the whole day stuck in my head, but it doesn’t feel like this constant heavy sadness sitting on me all day. It’s more like I’m preoccupied and tense, and that can make me seem low, maybe. My wife has asked if I’m okay because I’ll get quiet, but internally it’s not really that I’m sad in the way I think you mean. It’s more like I’m mentally elsewhere.

So… no, I haven’t noticed feeling depressed most of the day, nearly every day. At least not in a way I’d confidently call that.
